messages:

Subject: Increased latency & 5xx spike — need access logs and audit evidence

Hi David / Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated latencies and a spike in 5xx errors impacting several downstream jobs in our billing pipeline around 2026-03-09T22:08Z. Impact: several hourly jobs timed out and a handful of customer-facing requests experienced errors.

Immediate asks:
- Full request/host access logs for the window 2026-03-09T21:45Z -> 2026-03-09T22:30Z (request ids: r-8f3b2, r-8f3b7, r-8f3c1).
- Clarify what runtime data (KV cache contents, prefix caches, temporary traces) are persisted to object storage and for how long.
- Any audit evidence you can provide for access to customer data during the incident (who accessed logs, timestamps).

This is high priority for our internal postmortem and compliance lead — they may request the files as evidence for our internal SOC review. If you have a secure share/portal or preferred way to transfer redacted logs, let us know. Also please indicate if we need a legal/data processing agreement before you send anything.

Thanks,
Sara Johnson
Incident Lead, Clover Health
sara.johnson@cloverhealth.com
+1 415-555-0113

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 19:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Increased latency & 5xx spike — need access logs and audit evidence

David / team — status and proposed deliverable:

What we can provide within 24 hours:
- Request-level access logs for 2026-03-09T21:30Z -> 2026-03-09T22:45Z with fields: request_id, timestamp, route/model_version, response_code, node_id, latency_ms.
- GPU/node metrics and autoscaler events for the same window.
- Runtime trace snippets showing KV cache hit/miss rates (aggregated), not full cache dumps.

What we cannot provide raw (without review):
- Full request bodies (may contain PHI/PII).
- Internal debug traces that include token-level text.

Retention / persistence notes (for customer):
- Access logs (request metadata) are retained for 90 days by default in our central logging S3; encryption at rest (AES-256) and access logged via our IAM audit trail.
- KV cache is an in-memory construct; we do not persist per-request KV cache entries to S3. Periodic checkpoint metadata (non-user-content) is persisted for model optimizations and retained for 30 days.
- Audit logs for admin access to logs are stored for 365 days and include principal, action, resource, and timestamp.

Proposal to share evidence:
1) Produce redacted access logs (strip request bodies and user identifiers) and upload as a password-protected archive to our secure S3 share.
2) Provide an admin-audit excerpt showing who accessed the logs and when (timestamps + principal).
3) Include a short attestation PDF (signed by Security) that explains retention policy and the redaction performed.

I have prepared a partial export (redwood_runtime_logs_20260309.zip) — this is an encrypted, password-protected archive; Security will provide the password after approval. We will not include any unredacted request bodies.

Monica — need your sign-off to release the redacted archive to the customer.
Lauren — if legal wants a DPA tweak / formal agreement around transfer, let us know.

Vivek
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
